means:
Unshakeably calm; incapable of being agitated, flustered, or rattled.

The word only does its work when there's something to be rattled *by* — a crisis, an insult, a plane losing an engine. Plain **calm** describes a moment; **imperturbable** describes a temperament, a settled quality of the person. It leans admiring (the surgeon, the negotiator, the butler), but it can carry a faint chill too — someone so unmoved that you start to wonder whether anything registers at all.
trap: **imperturbable ≠ impertinent.** Same *imper-* opening, opposite social effect: *imperturbable* = unflappably composed; *impertinent* = cheeky, out of line. The imperturbable host smiles through the impertinent question.
trick_line: **Turbulence** hits everyone on the plane; the **imperturbable** passenger doesn't spill her coffee.
trick_unpack: The *turb* is literally *turbulence* — stirring, churning — and *im-* means it never gets through.
sentences: Under three hours of hostile cross-examination the witness remained **imperturbable**, correcting dates in the same flat voice she had used at the start.
Our nan is **imperturbable** — the oven caught fire and she just said "well, that's the pie done."
etymology: Latin **turbāre** = *"to stir up, throw into confusion,"* from **turba**, *"a crowd, an uproar."* Picture the disorder of a mob and the whole family opens up: **disturb**, **perturb**, **turbulent**, **turbid** (water stirred cloudy), **turmoil**, and even **trouble**. *Imperturbable* = the crowd cannot be made to churn.
one_line: Unshakeably calm; impossible to fluster, whatever happens.
root: turbāre (to stir up, disturb), from turba (crowd, uproar)
